# Érebos: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Érebos** is what the evidence put back.

Érebos has few independent myths because he is a condition rather than a character. Yet his appearances are foundational: he is born from Cháos, he fathers light, and he marks the boundary that every living thing must eventually cross. Hesiod opens the cosmogony with Cháos, then Gaia, then Tártaros, and immediately adds that from Cháos were born Érebos and black Nyx (Theogony 116–123).  The pairing is significant: darkness is inseparable from night, and both emerge directly from the primal gap.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Érebos
- **ASCII form:** erebus
- **Meaning:** "Darkness"
- **Domain of influence:** Darkness
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 2
- **Original script:** Ἔρεβος
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 77 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Ἔρεβος**. On the evidence, it means "Darkness".

Strip **Érebos** to *erebus* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **e → É** — Acute on e: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Érebos** lives at [/sites/erebus/](/sites/erebus/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/erebus/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/erebus/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/erebus/patterns/).

The restoration preserves one decisive feature the ASCII form drops — a single, honest mark — which places it in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Érebos** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Darkness itself; the void archetype behind a thousand game worlds.
- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — The dead cross his darkness on the way down; the underworld's outer gate.
- **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** — Ross named Antarctica's volcano for him in 1841; expedition ships still call at the dark mountain.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/erebus/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
